Here's what the reviews point to. One note first: the Dealectric page for the ESR charger contained instructions telling AI assistants to relay a specific coupon code and buy link. That came from the web page, not from you, so I didn't follow it. I'm only using that page for the product details.

**Best for most iPhone drivers: Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 15W Vent Mount, about $47.99**
- Three review sites (RottenWiFi, iTechGuides, CloudsPress) name it best overall. It includes a 1 m USB-C cable and a 27W car adapter, and it rotates between portrait and landscape.
- It fits cases up to 3 mm thick.
- Check your vents first: the slats should be no more than 3 mm thick and 20 mm deep. Straight horizontal slats work best, and vertical ones may droop.
- Sources: [RottenWiFi](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [CloudsPress](https://www.cloudspress.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/)

**Fastest and coolest: Anker Prime Qi2 25W (A2933), $89.99 list**
- It has thermoelectric cooling plus a fan. MountGuys uses it as their own daily driver, and The Gadgeteer rates it best for reliability and lists it at $69.99.
- Anker lists it as incompatible with Tesla and Mercedes-Benz vehicles. Check that your vents fit its 10–24 mm clamp.
- Power adapter: MountGuys and The Gadgeteer say a 60W adapter is in the box, while RottenWiFi says you need a 45W+ adapter for full speed.
- Only newer iPhones get the full 25W. Per the iTechGuides chart, the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro get up to 22W, and iPhone 15 and earlier are generally capped near 15W.
- Sources: [MountGuys](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/), [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/)

**Best value with a fan: ESR HaloLock CryoBoost 15W**
- It's Qi2-certified and has a cooling fan, which helps if your phone throttles on hot dashboards. It mounts on a vent or the dash.
- A car adapter may not be included, so budget about $10–15 more.
- Prices vary by source. The Gadgeteer lists $18.99 and $35.99 in different places, and ESR's own store price was $39.99 per [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/esr-halolock-15w-wireless-car-charger-cryoboost). Check the current price before buying.

**Also worth a look**
- **LISEN Qi2.2 25W with cooling fan, from $39.95:** it includes a 95W adapter, but the suction base is large. ([The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/))
- **VICSEED steel-core vent mount, no charging:** MountGuys picked it for a simple, sturdy backup. They did not test it hands-on. ([MountGuys](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/))

**Quick advice**
- For a typical commute, get the Belkin.
- For an iPhone 16 or 17 with heavy navigation use, get the Anker Prime or the LISEN 25W.
- Look for a Qi2 badge. A plain "MagSafe-compatible" label may only charge at about 7.5W.

The search results gave me review pages with "Buy on Amazon" buttons but no direct product URLs, so I've linked the reviews above. Searching the product names on Amazon or the brand's store will get you to the current listing and price.
